operations.comment: ; Local-only annotated AxROM source. Physical offsets include the 16-byte iNES header.
; Bank0..3 name 32 KiB images; effective 8 KiB contexts are [0..3], [4..7], [8..11], [12..15].
; Hardware, RAM and ROM are distinct spaces. Scratch RAM is reused by phase.
; Structural code does not establish natural selection or completion of a runtime wait.
; Validated 16-byte iNES header: AxROM mapper 7, 128 KiB PRG and CHR RAM.
; Disable interrupts and decimal mode, initialize the stack, disable rendering and wait for two
; vertical blanks before clearing the APU registers and RAM.
; Finish clearing APU register shadows, then clear zero page and stack RAM. Seed RAM00 with JMP
; opcode $4C so RAM01/02 can act as the bank-service trampoline.
; Install the RAM trampoline, initialize mapper/input/display state and compute the initial scene
; index. Synchronize display work before enabling the four APU channels.
; Keep the local high-score records when HighScoreSignatureLo/Hi contain AB/CD. Otherwise load the default
; screen and expand the seed records; $1F in the seed repeats across five fields.
; Copy encoded defaults backwards into HighScoreRecords onward, expanding the blank marker. Write the AB/CD
; signature and initialize the title countdown.
; Wait while the frame countdown is nonzero, then initialize rendering, player availability and
; the initial level/scene. Reset seeds X=2 and the countdown at its preceding setup.
; Preserve nonzero reserve counters and give an empty counter three entries before the next screen
; setup.
; Hide sprites, request palette synchronization, disable rendering and load scene graphics through
; banked services. Level selects a palette pointer; six spaced sprite records make the prompt.
; Alternate tile indices and copy six coordinate pairs into every other OAM record. Attributes are
; cleared.
; Wait for bit $10 in the combined newly pressed buttons before entering scene initialization.
; This polling loop depends on NMI controller updates.
; Check player availability, finish the current scene and either enter its boss at scene four or
; increment the scene and reload graphics.
; Call the boss sequence, then test player availability and advance the level or enter the ending.
; Artificial entry alone has not established a working boss state.
; After boss completion test remaining players. Level five enters the ending; otherwise reset
; scene to one, advance level and initialize the next presentation.
; Request a palette transition and call the illustrated ending. The artificial scenario renders
; this screen; natural progression to it remains unresolved.
; Clear player availability after the ending, disable background work and prepare the score
; display. Banked graphics setup precedes a Start-or-countdown wait.
; Wait for a newly pressed Start or expiry of the frame countdown. NMI must continue updating
; input and the countdown.
; Normalize the two player scores, run name entry for qualifying players and insert each result at
; its ranked position. Return through title presentation.
; A selects a player's three name bytes; X is the rank. Shift lower records down, then store name,
; six encoded score digits and a packed level/scene byte. The local offset table has five ten-byte
; records.
; Five byte offsets into the ranked ten-byte high-score records, used by insertion and
; lexicographic score comparison.
; X/Y form a zero-page pointer to six encoded score digits. Compare lexicographically against five
; ranked records; return rank 0..4 or $FF when none is lower. Equal scores continue to the next
; rank.
; Initialize scene state, enable display work and repeatedly update until the combined
; player/reserve test or scene counter ends the loop.
; Check two newly pressed button bytes for Start and an eligible player state. Save the streaming
; flag while an interlude runs; restore it before selecting the next sound request.
; Temporarily disable background streaming, initialize an audio sequence and wait for Start with a
; short software delay between updates.
; Nested X/Y delay followed by frame synchronization and a Start test. X is intentionally consumed
; by the delay.
; Set a pending music selection and restore the display-work flag before returning.
; A selects a music header. Initialize four channels at stride four with sequence pointers and a
; one-tick delay; clear modulation/envelope state. The tempo increment comes from the header
; table.
; Copy two pointer bytes per channel from the selected eight-byte header; channel RAM arrays are
; interleaved at offsets 0,4,8,12.
; Advance an eight-bit tempo accumulator and use its carry-derived sign to gate sequence ticks.
; Iterate four channels, servicing music and sound effects independently.
; On a tempo tick, decrement the note timer and parse the channel stream. Negative bytes select
; notes; nonnegative bytes dispatch commands. Outside a tick only modulation and register output
; are refreshed.
; Read at the stream pointer plus Y. Preserve Y while looking up note periods and restoring
; envelope/vibrato state.
; Set modulation counters and fetch the note timer low/high fields. The fourth channel uses a
; distinct period mapping for noise.
; Use an explicit duration byte unless a persistent duration is active, then advance the saved
; stream pointer past consumed bytes.
; Service channel timers, temporary signed pitch slides, oscillation and volume envelopes before
; writing APU shadows. Per-channel arrays use stride four.
; Restore the active signed pitch step, expire its duration and choose the reversed phase when its
; secondary counter is active. Add the sign-extended step to the channel's 16-bit period.
; At each reload interval add a signed step to the 11-bit timer and reverse the step after the
; configured run length.
; Gate envelope movement with per-channel counters and a target nibble. Stop the envelope when the
; low volume nibble matches its target.
; Restore the envelope endpoint and invert its movement counter to reverse the next envelope leg,
; then join the common register update.
; Force the next timer-high write and restore the channel sweep register after an effect releases
; the channel.
; Combine control bits with volume, write timer low, and write timer high only when it differs
; from the previous shadow. X is the APU channel stride.
; Select A as the effect for the first pulse channel; the common loader avoids restarting the same
; effect.
; Select the second pulse channel for the shared effect loader.
; Select the triangle channel for the shared effect loader.
; Select the noise channel unless its protected effect is already active.
; Use the even part of the effect selector as a pointer-table offset. Separate duration and
; control nibbles, copy sweep/timer shadows, then advance into the effect stream.
; Update the packed duration state and read the effect stream. A zero token releases the effect
; and restores music or silences the channel; other tokens provide volume and timer fields or
; dispatch commands.
; Extract volume and timer-high bits, preserving unrelated control bits. Write timer high only
; when the three low bits change; timer low is always written.
; Advance the effect pointer by Y plus one and propagate the page carry.
; Double the token into the adjacent 23-word handler table. Save X while loading the destination
; into scratch RAM and dispatch indirectly. Stream format supplies the selector; the table extent
; is established by handler boundaries rather than a selector mask.
; 23 little-endian audio command-handler pointers, bounded by first target $864C; two independent
; dispatch origins reviewed in contracts.md.
; Clear the music-active flag and enter the common silence path.
; Clear the effect control low bit and continue the shared effect parser after consuming the
; command.
; Disable the channel's persistent duration and resume the music parser.
; Read the next stream byte as the persistent note duration, then resume parsing.
; Read control, sweep and timer-high parameters from the stream, update volume state and resume
; token parsing.
; Store the volume and refresh the saved envelope start value when its high-bit mode is active.
; Read a little-endian destination from the bytecode stream, replace its pointer and resume at the
; new stream's first token.
; Read a repeat/count parameter, save the return pointer after the embedded destination, and
; replace the current stream pointer with that destination.
; Decrement the saved repeat count. Repeat the stored destination while nonzero; on expiry resume
; after its embedded two-byte address. X remains the channel stride.
; Read run length, reload delay and signed step parameters; initialize the step counters before
; resuming stream parsing.
; Clear the channel oscillation run length and resume token parsing.
; Read pitch-slide timing and step parameters, then use the positive step. The companion entry
; negates the step before joining the common store.
; Read slide parameters and negate the step, producing descending rather than ascending pitch
; motion.
; Consume reload interval, delay plus one and duration. Seed the live delay immediately; return
; the final byte as the signed step magnitude.
; Disable envelope movement and set a fixed volume nibble with its control bit.
; Clear the envelope start/enable state and resume the music parser.
; Preserve the initial volume and configure delay, reload interval and target volume from the
; stream.
; Configure envelope mode two, endpoint, half-endpoint and delay plus one, then join common
; envelope setup with the remaining stream parameter.
; Clear the channel envelope mode and resume token parsing.
; Use the next byte as the global music tempo increment. The additive entry starts with the
; existing increment, allowing relative tempo changes.
; Add the next stream byte to the current tempo increment through the common setter.
; Start the shared transpose command from zero; the relative entry instead starts from the current
; channel transpose.
; Add the next stream parameter to the per-channel note transpose, then resume parsing.
; Start with the current transpose and enter the additive transpose command.
; Copy one stream parameter to all four channel transpose fields, then continue parsing the
; current channel.
; Audio period words, sequence pointer directory and compact command streams; consumers
; $83BC/$83D5,$8554/$8559,$8313/$831F/$8325. Mixed adjacent formats remain Data without claiming
; individual full table domains.
; Mixed adjacent formats: this interval is not a single claimed asset. Consumer/boundary
; inspection is recorded in round002 review.md and residual-reference-review.json.
; Set both availability bytes to the $F2 sentinel and clear both reserve counters.
; Set both rendering-enable bits in the PPUMASK shadow.
; Run repeated frame/actor updates while clearing rectangle arrays. Release background states to
; their decay phase and wait until active actors and background objects disappear; final scene
; preserves its special slot-zero behavior.
; Start the initial audio sequence, prepare the title and test for eligible players/reserves
; before the next presentation routine.
; Check player state pairs and optionally trigger an effect. Return Z from the
; availability/reserve test; $F2 is the inactive sentinel.
; Play the pulse-two effect and return nonzero to the title availability test.
; Reset input overrides, blank rendering, load title graphics and synchronize. Run a bounded
; countdown while checking Start participation; then request a palette transition.
; Enable title display work and test newly pressed Start until participation or countdown
; expiration.
; Reset input overrides, blank rendering and run the timed title participation screen. Clear PPU
; increment mode while building the display and restore it on return.
; Blank rendering, clear PPU increment mode, load the score/title display and poll participation
; until accepted or the frame timer expires. Restore increment mode before returning.
; Check each controller's Start edge; initialize the selected player and set the other reserve
; counter. Return zero when accepted, $FF otherwise.
; Set level and scene to one, initialize status bytes with their sentinels, and clear eligible
; per-player action state.
; Start scene music, disable rendering and compute the doubled scene index. Load scene metadata,
; banked graphics and palette pointers; seed OAM helper records.
; Four-byte initial sprite0 OAM record copied by $8AA1 (Y=3 countdown).
; Initialize paired OAM attribute bytes, including horizontal flip for the mirrored half.
; Eight little-endian sprite-update handler pointers: AND7/ASL at $8AEB.
; Increment a rolling phase and dispatch through an eight-entry indirect table. Each phase handles
; part of the two-player sprite preparation.
; Set the PPU upload destination and convert the first player's current selector into a stream
; pointer.
; Save the previous selector, install the new one and choose tile indices for the first player's
; eight sprites.
; Set the PPU upload destination and resolve the second player's graphic selector.
; Save the second selector and assign a new eight-sprite tile sequence.
; Choose the alternate upload area for the first player's graphics.
; Install the first player's next graphic selector and alternate tile base.
; Choose the alternate upload area for the second player's graphics.
; Install the second player's next graphic selector and alternate tile base.
; Write eight tile indices at OAM stride four, increasing the tile by two for 8x16 sprites.
; Double the selector, index the word table at $C913 and replace the scratch pointer with the
; selected stream address.
; Select each player's pose list, optionally substitute the neutral pose, and expand up to eight
; coordinate pairs into OAM. Negative horizontal coordinates take the mirrored path; $FF hides the
; remaining records.
; Add pose offsets to the first player position. Negative Y offsets remain absolute; use palette
; zero.
; Fill unused OAM Y fields with $FF through the eight-sprite limit.
; Negate horizontal pose offsets around the player anchor. Retain negative hidden Y coordinates,
; apply mirrored attributes and emit eight sprite records.
; Read the mirrored vertical displacement, retaining negative hidden coordinates. Write the
; flipped attribute and advance four bytes to the next OAM record.
; Perform the analogous pose selection for the second player, using its own position and palette
; one.
; Expand coordinate pairs for the second player with a maximum sixteen-byte source span.
; Hide the remaining second-player OAM records until all eight slots are covered.
; Reflect X offsets around the second player anchor, retain negative hidden Y values and emit
; eight sprites with player-two palette and horizontal flip.
; Apply the same signed vertical-coordinate rule for player two, write palette plus horizontal
; flip and finish eight OAM records.
; Reset the PPU latch, write the destination and transfer exactly 128 bytes from the source
; pointer. Advance both source and destination by 128 with carry.
; Conditionally render player action indicators and a selected projectile marker. Coordinate
; offsets and blink phases come from small tables/frame bits.
; Use the selected slot's flags and frame bits to place an extra marker sprite.
; Turn frame bits into an OAM record index and reuse the action-marker writer.
; Small indexed selector/stride constants; $8D1C reads final two entries. Repeated even constants
; constrain non-code, exact subtable semantics unresolved.
; Clear each player's action state only when its availability byte is not the inactive sentinel.
; Reset both pose timers to $FF and clear auxiliary counters and graphic/background activity state
; shared by
; scene transitions.
; Reset presentation, start transition music and use bank-two services to initialize and finish
; the sequence. Continue frame updates until the active player's action state reaches $50; NMI and
; valid action initialization are prerequisites.
; Initialize boss-related counters, banked setup and staged transfers, then enter repeated
; updates. Required dependent state for an active boss remains unresolved; this is the mechanical
; contract only.
; Run updates until the frame countdown expires, then compute the scene index and invoke a banked
; setup service.
; Continue frame updates while the banked transfer counter remains nonzero, then request the
; second transfer.
; Wait for the second transfer to drain before continuing boss setup.
; Clear the background object selector, invoke bank-two boss setup and wait ten countdown ticks
; before selecting level-specific music.
; Refresh sprites, call banked boss behavior, update the common scene and test its
; completion/player state.
; Advance both players encoded completion counters, drain scene objects and handle the final-level
; actor/countdown wait before returning.
; Advance player-two status, drain scene objects and disable the boss display flag. Final level
; additionally releases the special actor and waits for its frame countdown.
; Increment a player's encoded status unless it is one of the two fixed sentinels $F2/$FB.
; Clear the transition scratch state, stop actor generation and use the common drain loop before
; proceeding to the next scene.
; Start ending music, load the ending graphics through a banked service and initialize
; palette/text transfer. The saved artificial route confirms this display, not natural
; reachability.
; Restore the row destination, fetch the next byte and queue it for NMI. A negative byte acts as a
; row control token; zero continues immediately.
; Synchronize frames around each queued byte. Negative control tokens advance the destination by
; one tile row; an eight-row countdown bounds the text block.
; Wait for the combined Start edge before requesting a palette transition.
; Clear the tall-sprite control bit and restore PPU address increment mode after ending text output.
; Convert twelve encoded score digits to the high-score alphabet, find both ranks and resolve
; their relative ordering. Pack qualifying rank plus one in two nibbles; $FF marks a player who
; did not qualify.
; A already contains PlayerOneRank, so this CMP compares that byte with itself.
; The next BNE cannot distinguish the two ranks; the six-digit comparison below
; still chooses insertion order even when the initial ranks differ. Bounded cases
; confirm 0/3 becomes 0/4 and 3/0 becomes 4/0: the lower-score candidate is shifted.
; Insertion later recomputes ranks at $81EC/$81FD. Intended design remains unresolved.
; Compare six player score digits to resolve insertion order, then increment the
; lower-score candidate's rank even when the initial ranks differ. Clamp ranks outside
; the five-entry table to $FF.
; Encode each nonnegative rank plus one into its player's nibble. Return zero when neither player
; qualifies.
; Prepare banked graphics, palette and two independent three-character name editors. Cursor values
; 1..33 select a grid or special action; each player's rank nibble enables its editor.
; Use directional edge bits to move through the five-column grid with explicit edge and
; special-action remapping. Inactive players retain cursor zero.
; Use parallel X/Y coordinate tables to arrange each player's cursor sprites. Map the selected
; grid index to a glyph or special-action icon.
; Observe held-button sign bits over a short frame window, retaining one selected glyph and
; release count per player. The counters distinguish an accepted press from a continuing hold.
; Ordinary glyphs update one of three name slots and advance the write cursor. Special selections
; clear, backspace or finish the editor; a negative write cursor means finished.
; Apply the same name-edit actions to player two's three-byte name buffer. Return to cursor
; polling until both write cursors are negative.
; Wait eighty synchronized frames, restore PPU increment mode and return through the common frame
; synchronization.
; Parallel 34-entry X and Y coordinate arrays for the name-entry cursor grid and its three special
; actions; used by both player editors.
; Return ordinary cursor indices directly; map indices $1F/$20 and the remaining special index to
; their display glyphs $49/$4C/$4F.
; Process both player coordinate pairs against fifteen enabled rectangles using coordinates
; divided by eight. Store the matched region index for subsequent collision handling.
; Skip players with an active indirect action; an input/state condition can enter the hit routine.
; Otherwise test an active player against rectangle bounds.
; Require an active player and graphic state, then normalize position to eight-pixel cells and
; scan enabled half-open rectangles.
; Process both player region markers. A negative marker selects a different update amount; region
; $0F means no contact.
; Decode the contact marker and update the selected player accumulator. Rectangle hits reduce
; health, release exhausted background state and generate contact effects before crediting the
; player.
; Use the decoded rectangle index to subtract damage from its enable/health byte. On exhaustion
; release its background state, handle the scene-$0C paired rectangle exception, spawn a visual
; effect at its center and credit the player's score accumulator.
; Reset scene counters and display flags, clear/setup OAM through banked helpers, initialize actor
; scripts and player coordinates, then enter a banked initialization service.
; Hide the actor sprite range before entering the common per-frame scene update.
; Disable NMI during main-thread scene work, rotate the update phase, maintain timers, update
; players/actors/collisions and banked services, then synchronize rendering at the frame boundary.
; Initialize contact sentinels, perform player and actor work, process pending music requests and
; update sprite/collision systems.
; Clear the global pending sound selector before joining the common update path.
; Derive progress from the initial and remaining counters, cap to the initial value, then update
; status counters and rendering.
; Wait for the sprite-zero status transition, apply a calibrated delay and optionally stream 128
; bytes to PPU; finally wait for NMI completion. Timing assumptions are NTSC baseline only.
; Initialize actors and display, stream banner graphics, build level/scene digit sprites and delay
; before enabling active scene flags.
; Set fixed banner tiles and convert one-based level/scene values to digit tile indices.
; Space banner sprites horizontally while skipping the center coordinate, then fill the two banner
; rows.
; Update frames until the countdown ends, restore scene flags and wait for the palette request to
; complete.
; HUD/text/PPU-address and sprite records with repeated triplets, pointer rows and constant
; columns. Consumers at $A241,$A278..$A309 and $809B; mixed format block retained as Data.
; Mixed adjacent formats: this interval is not a single claimed asset. Consumer/boundary
; inspection is recorded in round002 review.md and residual-reference-review.json.
; Install a two-byte activity timer and a frame mask controlling slower per-slot countdowns.
; Clear the two input override bytes so normal controller processing can run.
; Use A as the high PPU address byte and fix its low byte at $80.
; For inactive players with Start held, consume a nonzero reserve counter and initialize rejoining
; pose, graphic state and action delay.
; Initialize the player's core state, pose delay and inactive graphic selector before rejoining
; the shared player update.
; Preserve X, set an encoded availability state, initialize its action pointer sentinel and clear
; six encoded display/status bytes.
; Clear actor active fields, initialize six projectile Y slots and clear small effect state. $FF
; denotes an unused projectile.
; Compute scene metadata pointers and flags, initialize ten actor slots and expand four-byte
; records from a $FF-terminated list into parallel RAM arrays.
; Read position, type and script fields, preserve the script record address and advance to the
; next record until $FF.
; Clear two ten-entry actor-state arrays; X returns as $FF.
; Form a script address from each slot's saved relative pointer. $FF selects a new script or
; retires the slot; tokens $F0 and above use compact predefined records.
; Build the alternate script pointer using the table high byte and a fixed page displacement.
; Preserve bank/flag bits in the actor script state before joining common pointer processing.
; Expand shorthand tokens through three tables or consume a full three-byte state record. Certain
; kinds spawn auxiliary objects or projectiles.
; Optionally consume an extra state parameter, save the duration and advance the stored relative
; pointer by the consumed length.
; Clear actor packed motion, active state and extra state, then set its duration sentinel to $FF.
; Other actor-array fields retain their previous values until reallocated.
; Clear actor state and extra state, set its duration sentinel to $FF and return to the
; allocator's caller.
; Use the cyclic schedule cursor to find an available entry and expand its five-byte record. Avoid
; conflicting active kinds before entering the actor script parser.
; Scan other actor slots for the restricted kind range. On conflict mark the new kind invalid and
; continue the common allocation path; actor identities remain unresolved.
; Release the actor slot and assign its schedule-channel countdown five before continuing schedule
; processing.
; Load the schedule cursor for the shared advance/wrap/skip-actor tail. The complete
; load/increment/compare/wrap/store family also occurs at $98BC. The preceding
; terminal JMP and following INY bound this prefix; actual entry remains unobserved.
; For 1 <= count and cursor < count this BNE wrap agrees with the family's BCC.
; Special cursor overrides can exceed count (count 6, cursor 8), so that precondition
; is not a global invariant: here BNE retains 9 where BCC would wrap to zero.
; Increment the schedule index, wrapping only on equality with count, then skip this actor slot.
; Wait out the spawn delay, then process ten actor slots: parse expired scripts, advance motion,
; handle collisions and lifetimes, sort records and render grouped sprites.
; Duration zero requests the next script; $FF requests a schedule allocation. Other slots proceed
; with movement and rendering.
; Split the packed movement byte into direction components and use a four-phase delta table.
; Retire an actor that crosses the vertical bounds.
; Handle motion selector $88 using either direct stream positions or a scene-specific oscillation.
; Exact actor identity remains unresolved.
; Special kinds trigger projectile generation or a short horizontal separation test against other
; actors.
; Save the signed projectile slot selector; nonnegative selectors mark the corresponding
; projectile Y as $80 before resuming actor handling.
; Toggle bit seven in actor state and packed motion, then restart its duration at $50. Join the
; common actor continuation.
; Decrement nonnegative, nonzero durations once per eight-phase interval; continue through all ten
; slots.
; Perform adjacent swaps when vertical positions are out of order. Swap every parallel field
; together so scripts, lifetimes and positions retain slot identity.
; Alternate traversal direction each update and group nearby vertical positions. This changes
; sprite order to distribute OAM priority/flicker.
; Fill remaining sprite Y fields with $FF through the end of the OAM page.
; Two pairs of actor comparison/selection values read by $99CD/$9A00.
; Render the inclusive group in ascending or descending order according to the alternating phase
; flag.
; Update six projectiles and three small effects, choose a rotating OAM start, and render two
; transient effect records if active.
; Choose an animation list from the effect countdown, clamp Y, set palette/clip fields and call
; the common metasprite renderer.
; Low three lifetime bits gate motion. On tick seven use the upper lifetime bits to index parallel
; X/Y displacement tables and update the effect position.
; Set the sprite mode scratch byte to $80, call the shared metasprite renderer and join the
; auxiliary-object return path.
; Signed offset/velocity constants read by $9C19/$9C23.
; Scan three active slots. Stream-based modes emit clipped metasprites; simple modes select a
; direction/expiry tile and write one sprite. The OAM cursor stops on byte wrap.
; Read X displacement, tile and attributes from the selected stream and append an OAM record. Stop
; safely when the eight-bit OAM cursor wraps; preserve the outer object index on stack.
; Write object X and fixed palette. An expired/special object blinks with frame bit three;
; ordinary objects choose a tile from the direction of their remaining major-axis distance.
; Metasprite pointer bytes and repeated sprite records, consumed at $9CAF; prefix is split
; low/high pointer bytes rather than code.
; Preserve actor/script scratch and find one of three free slots. Initialize position from the
; actor, choose an available player target and derive signed line steps. Full pools leave existing
; objects unchanged.
; Copy actor Y, choose an available player with alternating frame parity and add a small
; frame-derived aim offset. Halve signed X distance and pass remaining vertical distance to the
; shared line-step initializer.
; Find a free slot among six projectile Y values, derive its kind from the actor type and
; initialize flags. Save/restore the caller's stream index.
; Compute projectile Y with an actor-relative offset and choose an available player. Set signed
; horizontal speed/flags according to which side of the player's anchor the actor occupies;
; preserve outer actor and script indices.
; For six slots, drain initial delay bits, integrate a signed fractional horizontal step and
; advance Y. Retire out-of-bounds projectiles, then test rectangle contacts and build OAM.
; Add the signed fractional step twice, propagating underflow/overflow into X. Advance Y once, or
; twice for one late-level slot.
; Mark the projectile Y as $FF and clear the selected-projectile marker when it refers to this slot.
; Convert coordinates to eight-pixel cells and test all fifteen enabled rectangles. Retire a
; projectile on a hit; follow with a banked service and OAM setup.
; Decrement the rectangle lifetime and clear its background state's high bit when the lifetime
; reaches zero.
; Alternate forward/backward OAM placement by frame parity, preserving position and
; selected-projectile effects.
; Occasionally copy selected projectile coordinates into a transient effect slot. Return an
; animated vertical offset for its sprite.
; Copy projectile Y into a transient effect slot, give it six ticks and restore the outer
; rendering index.
; Decode flags into a tile/attribute lookup. Delayed projectiles use a fixed marker and remember
; their slot for another sprite writer.
; Three indexed arrays of actor visual/selector constants, read at $9FD8/$9FDE/$9FF2.
; Select actor position, palette, tile base and animation list, account for region contact and
; scene flags, then call the common metasprite renderer.
; Discard hidden actors, decode kind and scene-dependent tile-bank selection, and prepare palette
; and animation flags.
; Handle region state and optional overlay graphics, then select a pointer list from kind and
; animation nibble. A zero animation falls back to a fixed list.
; Consume sprite triples until a negative leading byte. Offset Y above the anchor and X relative
; to it, clip horizontal wrap/range, apply tile base and attributes. X is the OAM cursor, Y the
; source index.
; Move clipped parts offscreen while still emitting the remaining sprite fields.
; Wrap the actor OAM cursor from $D4 to $C0 and save it for the next metasprite.
; Set horizontal flip, shift the anchor by eight and negate each relative X offset, retaining the
; same clipping rules.
; Write common attributes and tile plus base, then advance source by one and OAM by four.
; Five two-byte offset/size pairs read by $AF7A/$AF83; no invented game meaning.
; Prefer an inactive one of two effect slots; if both are active, alternate selection with frame
; parity.
; Call frame synchronization eighty times. Requires NMI progress; X is preserved by the frame
; service between countdown steps.
; Install the default palette pointer, set the pending flag and wait for NMI to clear it.
; Request the existing palette pointer and block until NMI services it.
; Toggle bit $10 in the mapper shadow; this chooses AxROM single-screen nametable selection.
; Toggle mapper bit $10 for AxROM single-screen nametable selection, then write through the
; matching ROM byte 00 or 10. Under the bank-zero entry contract lower bank bits remain unchanged.
; Z from the preceding toggle selects the ROM byte 00 at A20B or 10 at A20C. Writing A through
; that matching value avoids bus conflicts; these cartridge writes do not alter ROM.
; Two mapper-write values 00/10 used by $A203/$A207 at ROM addresses $A20C/$A20B; these are mapper
; writes, not self-modification.
; Disable display work, synchronize, toggle the mapper upper mode, synchronize again and restore
; the normal display-work flag.
; Tail-call bank-one service two through the common AxROM trampoline. The service restores the
; caller's physical bank before returning.
; Load bank-one service five, set the palette stream and write the high-score background. Decode
; packed level/scene nibbles into display glyphs, then build score/name sprites from the five
; ten-byte records.
; Walk thirty-four pointer/address pairs. Each points to a live glyph byte; write that byte to its
; PPU destination. Scratch pointers deliberately address both constants and computed RAM glyphs.
; Expand 29 three-byte layout records containing X, Y and score-buffer offset into OAM. Set
; palette zero and replace packed scene digits with separate tiles.
; Use packed ranking nibbles to select each player's score row and recolor three neighboring
; sprite attributes with player-specific palettes.
; Write palette A into three consecutive sprite attributes at the row-relative X offset.
; Split Y into two nibbles, add the digit tile base $1F and write two OAM tiles at X and X+4.
